ai.description: This caecilian reaches 15–20 cm in length with a uniform dark brown body. It is distinguished by a blunt, shovel-shaped snout and a lack of visible eyes, adapted for a fossorial lifestyle.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Humbarli Caecilian is best distinguished by its unique lack of secondary annuli, resulting in a smooth body surface compared to the ringed appearance of other species.
ai.habitat: *Indotyphlus maharashtraensis* inhabits moist, high-altitude evergreen forests in the Northern Western Ghats, typically found in leaf litter at elevations above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Humbarli caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows during heavy monsoon rains to forage for earthworms on the surface.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlus maharashtraensis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlus maharashtraensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Humbarli Caecilian produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of clicks or chirps, typically heard from within moist soil or leaf litter during the monsoon season.
